clips.text_zh: 成日都係咁。BTC 橫盤嗰陣冇人睇，一升15%就全部人衝入去。即係我哋呢啲散戶永遠都係接刀嗰個。prop firm 條數又難睇，考牌都未搞掂，仲有時間睇燭台。lol
clips.text_en_b1: You watch BTC do nothing for weeks and ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened? This came up on /biz/ today and anons are calling it classic FOMO behavior.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread mocking late FOMO buyers after a BTC pump
clips.text_en_b2: You sit around watching BTC grind sideways for weeks on end and couldn't care less. The moment it rips 15% higher, though, everyone suddenly rushes in trying to chase the move. Why does retail always end up catching the knife after the real damage is already done? It came up again on /biz/ today, and the anons are calling it textbook FOMO behavior — the same old cycle repeating itself over and over.
clips.text_en_c1: This pattern recurs with monotonous regularity. Whenever Bitcoin trades sideways for weeks on end, retail interest evaporates entirely; the moment a 15% move materialises, however, the same cohort that dismissed the asset rushes in headlong. It is the quintessential FOMO cycle, with retail invariably positioned to absorb the blow. Meanwhile, my prop firm statements remain an unreadable mess, the certification exam still looms, and the notion of scrutinising candlestick charts feels almost laughable. Such is the predicament of anyone foolish enough to attempt trading alongside a demanding professional workload. /biz/ has, predictably, already dismissed it as textbook herding behaviour.
clips.text_en_c2: It is, as ever, a tiresomely predictable pattern: BTC meanders sideways through weeks of consolidation, drawing scarcely a sidelong glance from the retail crowd, and the moment a fifteen-percent impulse arrives, the same erstwhile sceptics come flooding in with reckless alacrity. The asymmetry is rather telling; we plebeians invariably end up catching the blade, buying tops with metronomic precision while capital quietly rotates above us. Meanwhile, the prop firm evaluation remains an opaque gauntlet of arbitrary hurdles I have yet to negotiate, and licensure preparation continues to consume whatever cognitive bandwidth remains. Candlestick analysis, regrettably, has been relegated to the back burner, where it shall presumably languish until the next euphoric surge beckons. One can only laugh, lest one weep.

clips.text_zh: 認真笑唔出。我自己都試過，揸住個short冇set stop loss，睇住個位一直爆上去，加margin頂咗成個禮拜先至止蝕。搞到連bumble個女都唔想覆。廢柴。
clips.text_en_b1: Matched with a girl on Bumble a few weeks ago. Conversation was going well. Out of nowhere BTC started pumping, I shorted 72k with no stop loss and it kept pumping. Immediately lost all interest in girls. Continued adding margin for a whole week to avoid liquidation.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ poster blames BTC short squeeze for losing interest in dating
clips.text_en_b2: Honestly, I can barely even laugh at this one because I've been there myself. I was holding a short on BTC around 72k with absolutely no stop loss set, watching the price rip higher and higher while I kept throwing margin at it just to dodge liquidation for an entire week. The Bumble girl I had matched with? Completely ghosted me by the end. Absolute degenerate moment, and I still cringe thinking about it.
clips.text_en_c1: The situation strikes uncomfortably close to home, given I committed an analogous blunder mere weeks ago. A promising exchange with a woman on Bumble was progressing admirably until Bitcoin's sudden ascent compelled me to short the 72k region without setting a stop loss. As price ground relentlessly higher, my enthusiasm for romance evaporated entirely. Rather than capitulate, I opted to top up margin for the better part of a week, deferring the inevitable liquidation in the hope of mean reversion. Whether due to sheer obstinacy or terminal masochism, the outcome was the same: the position finally closed at a small loss, and my charisma remains entirely depleted.
clips.text_en_c2: The irony is almost too exquisite to bear. Some weeks ago, I was courting a rather promising Bumble match, the conversation humming along with all the requisite flirtatious momentum, until BTC inexplicably began a vertical ascent and I, in a moment of catastrophic hubris, shorted the 72k region without so much as a contingent stop-loss in place. The position bled mercilessly upward, and I found myself tethered to the margin dashboard, haemorrhaging collateral for what felt like an eternity before capitulating a full week later, thoroughly liquidated in spirit if not in ledger. The girl, predictably, stopped replying. One cannot help but observe that the market's capacity for personal devastation is, in its own grim way, rather sublime.

clips.text_zh: 有時我會諗，啲GPU咁重要，點解仲到我哋呢啲散戶買得到？AI 大戰打到咁，政府同企業全部掃緊貨，但個價錢貴歸貴，貨源居然仲有。到底係產能真係咁勁，定係啲大deal未真正落地？
clips.text_en_b1: Every government and corporation wants its own AI. Why are GPUs and RAMs still available for normal people to buy? They are extremely expensive, but we can still buy them. If AI is as important as people say, GPUs and RAM should already be out of stock.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread questioning why GPUs are still purchasable during the AI boom
clips.text_en_b2: It genuinely makes me pause for thought sometimes — if GPUs and RAM are supposedly so critical to the whole AI arms race, how come ordinary consumers can still get their hands on them without much hassle? Every government and major corporation out there is snapping up stock, yet somehow the shelves are not empty. Either production capacity is far better than people assume, or those massive enterprise deals have not actually materialized yet.
clips.text_en_c1: It is a question that occasionally surfaces in my reflections. If artificial intelligence carries the strategic weight that governments and Fortune 500 corporations evidently believe it does, why on earth are high-end GPUs and memory modules still purchasable by ordinary consumers? Both remain prohibitively expensive, admittedly, yet consistent availability at stated prices implies either that fabrication capacity has surged beyond prevailing estimates or that the much-vaunted hyperscaler deals have not translated into actual binding orders. Until the order books corroborate the rhetoric, this apparent accessibility warrants closer examination rather than uncritical acceptance.
clips.text_en_c2: It is a question that nags at me with increasing insistence: if sovereign governments and multinational corporations are, as we are ceaselessly told, engaged in an existential scramble for AI supremacy, why on earth are GPUs and high-bandwidth memory still ostensibly procurable by ordinary consumers at retail? The prevailing narrative suggests that silicon should be vanishing from shelves the moment it leaves the foundry, yet inventory persists, prices stratospheric though they may be. Either production capacity has scaled beyond even the most optimistic forecasts, or the much-vaunted enterprise deals remain, for the moment, aspirational rather than contractual. The disconnect between rhetoric and supply chain reality is, to put it mildly, rather curious.

clips.text_zh: 呢篇pol講印度移民喺歐美嘅犯罪率同經濟貢獻，數字睇落好靚。但我唔太buy，data 點收集、點分類先係重點。香港就唔同講法啦，呢度講緊另一個story。wtf
clips.text_en_b1: Indians are always among the groups with the lowest crime rates of all, along with Chinese. Net economic contribution data from the Netherlands, Denmark, UK, Germany and the US also shows positive numbers for Indians. The US does not have a separate figure for Indians, just the broader Asian category.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread arguing Indians have strong economic and crime stats abroad
clips.text_en_b2: Indians consistently rank among the lowest-crime demographic groups, alongside Chinese populations across most datasets. Net economic contribution figures from the Netherlands, Denmark, the UK, Germany, and the United States also paint a rather favorable picture, though the US only lumps Indians into the broader Asian category rather than breaking them out separately. The way the data has been gathered and classified is arguably far more telling than the headline numbers themselves.
clips.text_en_c1: The thread purports to demonstrate, with admirable statistical restraint, that Indian immigrants post remarkably low crime rates alongside ethnic Chinese populations and contribute positively to GDP across the Netherlands, Denmark, the United Kingdom, and Germany. Comparable American figures are regrettably absent, with Indians subsumed within the broader Asian category. While the data appears compelling at first glance, methodology ought to temper enthusiasm, since collection techniques, classification criteria, and reporting incentives vary considerably between jurisdictions. Hong Kong constitutes an entirely separate analytical case, of course, and the prevailing narrative there bears little resemblance to that propagated by Western think tanks.
clips.text_en_c2: A pol thread circulating aggregated crime statistics and net fiscal contribution data for Indian diaspora communities across the Netherlands, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Germany, and the United States presents figures that, at surface level, appear commendably favourable, situating Indians alongside Chinese populations among the lowest-crime cohorts. The Netherlands, Denmark, the UK, and Germany furnish discrete datasets; the United States, regrettably, subsumes Indians within a vaguer 'Asian' taxonomic bracket, which rather muddies comparative analysis. Whether one finds these numbers persuasive depends, as ever, on the methodological scaffolding beneath them: how incidents are classified, how ethnicity is recorded, which confounding variables are excluded. Polished statistics, after all, rarely survive close scrutiny of their provenance.

clips.text_zh: S15 開季冇時間睇，反而GTA6個Lucia被人話woke lol。5呎2吋女仔一拳打暈6呎3吋男人？呢啲我哋打LOL嗰陣見慣啦，relatable。考牌溫書溫到腦閉塞，要啲垃圾content抖下。
clips.text_en_b1: GTA 6 is fine but Lucia is immersion breaking. A 5 foot 2 girl can knock out a 6 foot 3 man with one punch, can shoot and drive at superhuman levels, and even reloads shotguns with one hand. Anons in the thread are calling this nonsense and blaming it on wokeness.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread complaining that Lucia breaks immersion in GTA 6
clips.text_en_b2: GTA 6 itself looks solid enough, but Lucia genuinely breaks the immersion for me. A five-foot-two woman knocking out a six-foot-three man with a single punch, handling shotguns one-handed, and pulling off superhuman driving stunts — that is the kind of nonsense we routinely laugh at in League of Legends, not what we want from a grounded crime sandbox. The thread is full of anons pinning the absurdity squarely on wokeness rather than weak writing.
clips.text_en_c1: GTA VI is shaping up splendidly, though the characterisation of Lucia has drawn considerable ire from the playerbase. A woman standing five foot two allegedly flooring a man of six foot three with a single blow strains credulity to breaking point. Compounding matters, she reportedly reloads shotguns one-handed, drives at apparently superhuman speeds, and wields firearms with mechanical precision. Anons across the thread have attributed these absurdities to the prevailing influence of corporate diversity initiatives. Whatever the underlying rationale, the immersion, as critics contend, suffers considerably. Midterms beckon, and such distractions provide welcome relief from relentless study.
clips.text_en_c2: GTA VI's Lucia has, predictably, become the latest crucible for the culture war faithful, with anons brandishing the familiar accusations of 'wokeness' as though the label itself constituted a substantive critique. The alleged affront is, ostensibly, immersion-breaking: a five-foot-two woman dispatching a six-foot-three adversary with a solitary blow, performing superhuman feats of marksmanship and automotive dexterity, and casually racking a shotgun one-handed. To anyone who has spent considerable hours in League of Legends, such exaggerated power fantasies scarcely register as remarkable; they are, in fact, rather relatable. Whether the design choice constitutes artistic license or pandering remains contested, though one suspects the discourse itself is the actual product.

clips.text_zh: 睇到呢篇fit諗起自己。三個月減45磅係好勁，但肌肉同力量一齊冇埋真係worst。肥仔信今日又tag我上gym，我而家只想食返飽先算。ok 之後再算。
clips.text_en_b1: Lost 45 pounds in 3 months but definitely lost muscle and strength. Being at the gym kills me now. I cannot go hard or lift heavy because my body will not let me. I get fatigued as fuck, my heart gets destroyed by squat sets, and I can barely eat more than a couple times a day.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about losing strength while cutting weight fast
clips.text_en_b2: Reading that thread took me right back to my own cut. I dropped a solid 45 pounds in roughly three months, which sounds impressive until you factor in the muscle and strength I shed along the way — that is genuinely the worst part nobody warns you about. Walking into the gym now is a slog; I cannot push heavy sets without my body giving out, my heart gets wrecked by squat volume, and forcing down more than a couple of meals a day is…
clips.text_en_c1: That thread prompted uncomfortable self-reflection. Shedding forty-five pounds within a mere three months is undeniably impressive, but the concurrent erosion of muscle mass and measurable strength represents a Faustian bargain at best. The gym, once a sanctuary, has become an ordeal, since my constitution simply will not tolerate the requisite intensity. Squat sets send my heart rate into palpitations; even moderate exertion leaves me utterly depleted; and caloric consumption beyond twice daily feels insurmountable. A friend tagged me earlier this morning, oblivious to the wreckage he was reminding me of. Recovery, one supposes, precedes further endeavour.
clips.text_en_c2: A thread on fit detailing an agonising three-month descent from obesity, during which the protagonist shed a staggering forty-five pounds, resonated with uncomfortable precision, chiefly because the collateral damage was conspicuously familiar: muscle catabolism, precipitous strength attrition, and a metabolic profile now utterly unsuited to exertion. The gym, once a sanctuary, has become something approaching punitive; heavy compound movements provoke cardiac arrhythmias, squat racks induce exhaustion bordering on collapse, and appetite has dwindled to a miserly twice-daily affair. A rotund acquaintance, whose encouragement was never solicited, has once again issued an exhortation to train, though the present inclination is rather more caloric than catechismic. Tomorrow, perhaps, discipline shall return.

clips.text_zh: 終於有人講句公道話。Mobile Suit Gundam 真係神作，而家啲人成日要連Zeta、ZZ、CCA一齊講，act as if 同一個team做。搞到我哋00 fans好撚嬲。美國佬特別鍾意Zeta我都唔明，OK？
clips.text_en_b1: Is Mobile Suit Gundam underrated? Nowadays most people cannot discuss it without mentioning Zeta, ZZ, and CCA, which were made by completely different people and should be considered non-canon. Americans in particular are bizarrely obsessed with Zeta, which was quite disliked when it first aired.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread arguing the original Mobile Suit Gundam is underrated compared to its sequels
clips.text_en_b2: Finally someone in that thread is speaking a bit of sense. The original Mobile Suit Gundam remains an absolute masterpiece, yet nowadays nobody seems capable of discussing it without bundling Zeta, ZZ, and CCA into the conversation as though they were all produced by the same team. As a Gundam 00 fan, that honestly drives me up the wall. The American obsession with Zeta in particular is baffling, given how poorly received it was when it originally aired.
clips.text_en_c1: At last, someone articulates the obvious. The original Mobile Suit Gundam stands as an unparalleled achievement in the medium, yet contemporary discourse routinely conflates it with Zeta Gundam, ZZ, and Char's Counterattack, as though these productions emerged from the identical creative team. Such conflation is intellectually inexcusable, given that Tomino's involvement varied significantly between projects, and later instalments have historically been contested as non-canonical. American audiences in particular display a peculiar fixation upon Zeta, which Japanese viewers received with markedly less enthusiasm upon its initial broadcast. Fans of Gundam 00 can only observe such collective myopia with considerable exasperation.
clips.text_en_c2: It is, at last, a modicum of critical justice: someone has deigned to articulate that Mobile Suit Gundam, the ur-text of the entire mecha genre, remains chronically undervalued in contemporary discourse. The prevailing tendency to bundle it indistinguishably with Zeta, ZZ, and Char's Counterattack, as though these constituted a unified auteur project, is intellectually indefensible, given that entirely different creative teams helmed each successive production. That these later entries should be treated as canonical scripture is, frankly, preposterous. American audiences, in particular, evince a bafflingly ardent attachment to Zeta, a series which, lest we forget, was received with marked ambivalence upon its original broadcast. The double standards are, as ever, rather pronounced.
